column1: # Engine-parity regression classes, from the boru differential-probe report
# against @tabnas/parser + @tabnas/jsonic (fixed upstream in parser 0.8.0 /
# jsonic 0.6.0). These pin how each class manifests through aontu's OWN
# semantics — where the engine's old defects variously fabricated list
# elements, destroyed characters, or silently swallowed separators, aontu
# must instead give either a clean value or a clean aontu error.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect ; mode: canon|gen|err
# Base-prefixed run with a dot continuation: lexes as TEXT whole (engine
# adjudication), and a bare dotted word in aontu is a path REFERENCE — so
# these resolve like any other unresolvable ref: a clean no_path/negative
# error, identical to a:[zz.qq]. The old TS engine fabricated elements here
# ([0xFF.5] parsed as [[],"xFF.5"]) and destroyed the leading character.
prefix-dot-ref-err
prefix-dot-ref-err2
prefix-dot-ref-neg
prefix-dot-ref-same
# Separator at a run edge: not a number (engine adjudication: separators
# only between digits). The old Go engine parsed +_1 as the NUMBER 1,
# silently changing user data; 1_ as 1.
sep-edge-str
sep-edge-list
# Unary + on a non-number is aontu's expr semantics (the operator yields
# its operand), NOT character corruption: +x behaves identically.
sep-edge-unary
unary-plus-word
unary-plus-num
# Protected baselines: interior separators and base-prefixed literals.
baseline-sep
baseline-hex
baseline-hex-list
# Integer-like keys: generated JSON enumerates them ascending (a JS/plain
# representation semantic on both ports; source order is not preserved in
# gen output).
intkey-order
